The Education

Why ESRD Billing Is the Most Specialized Medicare Payment System in Outpatient Medicine

Nephrology billing covers the complete spectrum of kidney disease management from early CKD office visits through ESRD dialysis billing, transplant management, and the newest revenue category: remote patient monitoring for CKD patients not yet on dialysis.

The ESRD Monthly Capitation Payment (MCP) is Medicare's bundled payment for the nephrology physician's professional services related to dialysis treatment. The MCP is billed per patient per month with specific codes for in-center hemodialysis (90960-90962 based on visit frequency) and home dialysis (90963-90966 for PD, 90967-90970 for home HD). Getting the MCP code correct requires knowing the actual number of face-to-face visits the nephrologist had with the patient during the month not the number of dialysis sessions.

The most common nephrology billing error: a nephrologist visits the dialysis unit three times in the month. The correct MCP code is 90960 (4+ visits/month). Billing 90962 (1 visit/month) instead means receiving $170 instead of $400 per patient per month. Across a panel of 100 ESRD patients, that systematic MCP miscoding costs $276,000 annually.

CKD remote patient monitoring is the fastest-growing new revenue program in nephrology. Hypertension monitoring with connected blood pressure devices, fluid balance monitoring, and kidney function tracking generate RPM billing (99453, 99454, 99457, 99458) that most nephrology practices have not implemented despite having large, qualifying CKD panels.

The Highest Per-Patient Monthly Error in Nephrology Billing

The ESRD Monthly Capitation Payment vs. Individual Visit Coding Error

The MCP system pays nephrologists a monthly bundled rate for managing ESRD patients but the rate depends on how many face-to-face patient visits occurred in the dialysis unit that month. The code tiers are: 90960 (4+ visits), 90961 (2-3 visits), 90962 (1 visit). Each tier pays significantly differently 90960 pays approximately $400/month, 90962 pays approximately $170/month. The difference per patient per month is $230.

The most common error: billing 90962 (1 visit/month) by default across all ESRD patients either because the billing team does not track actual visit counts, or because they assume the minimum to avoid scrutiny. For a nephrologist seeing 100 ESRD patients monthly with an average of 3 visits per patient, defaulting to 90962 instead of 90961 costs $23,000 per month $276,000 per year from one wrong code applied systematically.

PMEx tracks face-to-face visit documentation for every ESRD patient every month, determines the correct MCP tier from the visit log, and submits the accurate MCP code recovering the full value of the physician work performed without any overcoding risk.

EPO Auth Gap

Erythropoietin Administered Without Active Authorization

EPO (J0885/J0886) or darbepoetin administered to ESRD patient. Authorization expired. Commercial payer denies high-cost drug claim retroactively.

PMEx tracks EPO authorization renewal cycles and submits renewals 30 days before expiration. Every ESA administration has active confirmed authorization.

Home Dialysis Error

Home PD or HD Billed with In-Center Codes

Patient on home peritoneal dialysis billed with in-center hemodialysis codes. Medicare processes differently home dialysis MCP codes require documentation of monthly management visits and home training completion.

PMEx verifies dialysis modality for every ESRD patient monthly and applies correct MCP code set in-center HD (90960-90962), home PD (90963-90966), home HD (90967-90970).

Post-transplant nephrology visits managing immunosuppression, rejection monitoring, and complications coded at 99213 when 99215 is supported by clinical complexity.

PMEx reviews transplant management visit documentation against 2021 AMA MDM criteria applying level 5 when immunosuppression management, rejection risk assessment, and lab interpretation support it.
